items.prompt: One leaf, two ___.

options.why: Leaf changes its f to v before adding -es.
The f changes to v before the ending.
This is missing the e.

hints: Leaf ends in f.
Many words ending in f change the f to v and add -es.
Think of half and halves.
items.explanation: Leaf ends in f, so we change the f to v and add -es: leaves.

items.prompt: One shelf, three ___.
hints: Shelf ends in f.
Change the f to v.
Then add the same ending as in leaves.
items.explanation: Shelf changes f to v and adds -es: shelves.

items.prompt: Match each word to its plural.
hints: These words change in other ways to make a plural.
Say each one aloud: one child, two ...
Start with foot. What do you call two of them?
items.explanation: These are irregular plurals. They change inside the word or become a new word, like child and children.

items.prompt:
Write the plural of loaf.
The baker took six ___ of bread out of the oven.
hints: Loaf ends in f.
Words like leaf and loaf change the f.
Change the f to v, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Loaf ends in f, so it becomes loaves.

items.prompt: Sort the words by how they make their plural.
hints: Say each plural aloud.
Do you hear a v sound in the plural?
Start with roof. Do we say roofs or rooves today?
items.explanation: Wolf, half, life and calf change to -ves. Roof, chef, cliff and giraffe just add -s.

items.prompt: There are many ___ in the farmer's field.

options.why: Sheep stays the same for one or many.
There is no -es. The word never changes.
Shoop is not a word.

hints: Some animals have the same word for one and for many.
Think of one fish, two fish.
Which word does not change at all?
items.explanation: Sheep is the same in the singular and the plural: one sheep, many sheep.

items.prompt: Which plural is spelt correctly?

options.why: Tomato needs -es at the end.
This is missing the s.
Tomato does not end in y.

hints: Tomato ends in o.
Some words ending in o add -es.
Think of potato and potatoes.
items.explanation: Tomato adds -es: tomatoes. Potato and hero do the same.

items.prompt:
Write the plural of goose.
A family of ___ walked across the road.
hints: Goose has an irregular plural.
Think of tooth and teeth.
Change the oo sound in the middle.
items.explanation: Goose has an irregular plural, geese, just like tooth becomes teeth.

items.prompt: Which sentence has every plural spelt correctly?

options.text: The childs put the loaves on the shelfs.
options.why: Child becomes children, and shelf becomes shelves.

options.text: The children put the loafs on the shelves.
options.why: Loaf becomes loaves.

options.text: The childrens put the loaves on the shelves.
options.why: Children is already plural. It does not need an s.

options.text: The children put the loaves on the shelves.

hints: There are three plurals in each sentence.
Check the plural of child, then loaf, then shelf.
Remember that some plurals do not end in s at all.
items.explanation: Child becomes children, loaf becomes loaves and shelf becomes shelves.

items.prompt:
Write the plurals of calf and pony.
Two ___ and three ___ ate grass in the field.
hints: You need two plurals.
Calf ends in f. Pony ends in a consonant and y.
Do calf first. What happens to the f?
items.explanation: Calf changes f to v: calves. Pony changes y to i and adds -es: ponies.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that are the same in the singular and the plural.

options.why: One goat, two goats.
One cow, two cows.

hints: Say each word with one and then with two.
Does the word change at all?
Try sheep: one sheep, two ...?
items.explanation: Sheep, fish and deer stay the same: one deer, two deer. Goat and cow add -s.

items.prompt: Which word breaks the -ves rule and just adds -s?

options.why: Loaf becomes loaves.
Half becomes halves.
Wolf becomes wolves.

hints: All four words end in f.
Say each plural aloud.
Listen for a v sound. Which plural keeps an f sound instead?
items.explanation: Roof just adds -s: roofs. Loaf, half and wolf change f to v and add -es.

items.prompt: One child, two ___.

options.why: Child is an irregular noun. It does not take -s.
Children is already plural. Do not add -s.
Check the letters in the middle: there is an r.

hints: This noun does not follow the usual -s rule.
Think of a word you say about a class.
Say: one child, two ...
items.explanation: The plural of child is children. It is an irregular plural.

items.prompt: One baby, many ___.

options.why: Baby ends in y after a consonant, so y changes.
We do not keep y and add -es.
Babis misses the letters ie.

hints: Look at the last letter of baby.
The letter before y is a consonant.
Change y to i and add -es.
items.explanation: Baby ends in y after a consonant, so y changes to i and we add -es: babies.

items.prompt:
Write the plural of box.
The shop had three big ___ of apples.
hints: Look at how box ends.
Words ending in x need more than -s.
Add -es.
items.explanation: Words that end in x, s, sh or ch add -es: boxes.

items.prompt: The farmer has two ___ and five ___ in the barn.
hints: One of these nouns stays the same.
The other changes its vowels.
Think of a shy animal and a woolly animal.
items.explanation: Sheep stays the same in the plural. Mouse changes to mice.

items.prompt: Match each word to its plural.
hints: These do not follow the add -s rule.
The vowels change.
Start with tooth. Think of oo.
items.explanation: These are irregular plurals. The vowels change instead of adding -s.

items.prompt:
Write the plural of church.
The two ___ in the village are very old.
hints: Look at the last two letters of church.
Words ending in ch add more than -s.
Add -es.
items.explanation: Church ends in ch, so we add -es: churches.

items.prompt: Sort the words by how they make their plural.
hints: Look at the letter before y in toy and city.
A vowel before y means we just add -s.
Start with dish. Is it dishs or dishes?
items.explanation: Toy and day have a vowel before y, so they add -s. City and story change y to ies. Bus and dish add -es.

items.prompt: Which pair is correct?

options.why: Photo is short for photograph and only needs -s.
Piano only needs -s.
Zoo ends in two o letters and only needs -s.

hints: Some words ending in o add -es, and some only add -s.
Think of food words for -es.
Check each one by saying it aloud.
items.explanation: Tomato adds -es. Photo, piano and zoo only add -s.

items.prompt: Spell the plural of woman.
items.sentence: The women walked to the market together.
hints: This plural does not end in s.
Only the vowel in the middle changes.
Change the a to e.
items.explanation: The plural of woman is women. The vowel changes.

items.prompt: Which sentence has a plural mistake?

options.text: The sheeps ate grass all morning.
Two deer drank at the river.
options.why: Deer stays the same in the plural. This one is fine.
Mice is the correct plural of mouse. This one is fine.
Men is the correct plural of man. This one is fine.

hints: Think about which nouns do not take -s.
One animal in the sentences stays the same.
Check the animal words first.
items.explanation: Sheep stays the same in the plural, so sheeps is wrong.

items.prompt: Choose all the plurals that are spelt correctly.

options.why: Baby changes y to ies.
Wolf changes f to ves.
Dish needs -es.

hints: Look at the end of each singular word.
A vowel before y just adds -s.
Words ending in f or fe often change to ves.
items.explanation: Monkeys, tomatoes and lives are correct. Babys, wolfs and dishs need ies, ves and es.

items.prompt: Build a sentence about farm animals. Use two irregular plurals.
items.answer: The two geese chased three mice.
hints: It starts with The.
Both animals change their spelling.
Put the number words before the animals.
items.explanation: Geese and mice are irregular plurals.

items.prompt:
Write the plurals of wife and tomato.
The ___ bought ten ___ at the market.
hints: Fill the first gap, then the second.
Wife ends in fe and changes.
Change f to v and add -es for wife. Add -es for tomato.
items.explanation: Wife changes to wives, and tomato takes -es.

items.prompt: Which pair of words both change f to v in the plural?

options.why: Roofs and cliffs just add -s.
Chefs and chiefs just add -s.
Leaf changes, but roof just adds -s.

hints: Say each plural aloud.
Only some f words change.
Check roof first. It is a surprise.
items.explanation: Wolves and calves change f to v. Roofs, cliffs, chefs and chiefs just add -s.

items.prompt:
Write the plural of half.
The cake was cut into two ___.
hints: Look at how half ends.
Many words ending in f change.
Change f to v and add -es.
items.explanation: Half changes f to v and adds -es: halves.

items.prompt: Which word ends in s but is NOT a plural?

options.why: Boys is plural. It means more than one boy.
Cats is plural. It means more than one cat.
Dishes is plural. It means more than one dish.

hints: Think about meaning, not just spelling.
A plural means more than one.
Which word names just one thing?
items.explanation: Bus is singular. It names one vehicle even though it ends in s.

items.prompt: Which sentence is about only one animal?

options.text: The sheep are in the field.
options.why: Are shows there is more than one sheep.
Were shows there is more than one deer.
Mice is already plural.

hints: Some nouns look the same as singular and plural.
Look at the verb after the noun.
Is, was, are or were?
items.explanation: Is shows one. Sheep and deer stay the same, so the verb tells us the number.

items.prompt:
Write the plurals of leaf and roof.
Autumn ___ covered the ___ of the houses.
hints: Fill the gaps in order.
Both words end in f, but only one changes.
Leaf changes to ves. Roof just adds s.
items.explanation: Leaf changes to leaves. Roof is an exception and just adds -s: roofs.
